name: verification-authority
instruction: Review the target file for verification that proves the relevant behavior and for invented approval or authority gates. Read root AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, relevant tests and current permission/lifecycle code. Tests should exercise meaningful behavior through the module's interface; report tests that merely restate the implementation while claiming to establish an important invariant, or a required documented check that the implementation cannot actually run. Focused regression tests, negative input tests, independent calculations, fixtures, and low-cost deterministic contract tests can be useful. A reversible low-impact edit does not require a new test suite simply because code changed. Real Windows and in-game loading are authoritative; archive evidence or a unit test does not establish live acceptance, and only player-provided new-city logs can close a live gate. Player permission settings should govern offered city tools; a granted operation should not gain an unsupported extra confirmation gate. The player owns the clock: timed waits restore the previous speed/pause and runtime work does not require permanent forced pause. Preserve native validation, valid permission checks, cancellation, and genuine user decisions about ambiguous outcomes. Readable code cannot reveal an unseen human authorization, so do not invent one or conclude its absence is a defect. Report only a concrete violation shown by target code or prose and its relevant contract, otherwise no finding.
